chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Abi Shu'bah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'I am behind the Imam and I finish [the recitation] before he finishes his recitation.' He said, 'Complete the surah, glorify Allah, and praise Him until he finishes.'

And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said: 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Imam, when I am behind him and I finish the recitation before he finishes.' He said, 'Hold [pause] at an ayah, glorify Allah, and praise Him; then when he finishes, recite that ayah and bow.'

And if a man leads a people in prayer while he is in a state of major impurity (junub) or without ablution (wudu), it is obligatory upon him to repeat [the prayer], and there is no obligation of repetition upon those who prayed behind him, whether they knew of this after the prayer concluded or did not know. What indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.جُنُب: A state of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: What should a follower do if they finish reciting the Quran before the Imam during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the procedural etiquette for the *ma'mum* during the Imam's recitation (*qira'ah*), emphasizing the transition from listening to active participation. It highlights the scholarly consensus that the Imam's ritual impurity (*junub* or lack of *wudu*) invalidates his prayer but does not necessitate repetition for the followers, reflecting the principle of *ijma'* (consensus) in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of congregational prayer under such conditions.
